## Summary

I implemented F015 — the skill auto-run ALLOWLIST artifact and approval gating that the F011 evaluator consults via its injected predicate. The new `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/skill_allowlist.py` defines a versioned, content-hashed, auditable `skill-autorun-allowlist.json` artifact (each entry records skill name, exact command_template *or* command_prefix, an auto-only `allowed_mode`, owner/approved_by/approved_at metadata, and rationale), a `classify_allowlist()` that reports `missing/unloadable/stale/conflicting/ok`, and `build_predicate()` — the `is_command_allowlisted` callable F011 injects. The predicate authorizes a command **only** when the allowlist is trusted (status OK), an entry matches the exact/prefix command, and that entry carries no risk flag; a missing/stale/conflicting/unloadable allowlist (or any risk-flagged entry) denies everything, so mutating/credentialed/networked/paid/external-write/indefinite-loop skills are never silently executed (AC4/AC7). For visibility (AC5) I added a `provider_skill_allowlist` to the F008 config inventory (with a matching non-optimistic-status invariant case so a stale/conflicting allowlist never reports `ok`), a `check_skill_allowlist()` doctor check wired into `check_agent_onboarding` (missing→OK advisory, stale/conflicting→WARN, unloadable→FAIL), and added the allowlist filename to `home_reconcile.RECONCILE_FILENAMES` so `reconcile homes` surfaces legacy-only/divergent allow
